source_text:
# BUG#28 (QualityControl ledger) — REGRESSION FIXTURE for the ordering
# pair a BUG#4-shaped mistake would land on: a creating command that is
# BOTH `complete_state?` AND `state_independent?` (`Vault.Open` sets
# every owner field straight from its own arguments, no `given` at all)
# paired with an aggregate-level invariant that is GENUINELY FALSIFIABLE
# at creation — unlike the real corpus's own one example of this shape
# (`Banking::Account.Open`'s "the balance never goes negative": `Account`
# never sets `:balance` in `Open` and `Money.cents` defaults to 0, so
# that invariant can never actually fail there today). Here, `balance`
# IS a required, caller-supplied argument with no non-negative
# constraint of its own, so a caller can genuinely violate "a vault's
# balance never goes negative" at the exact moment it's created.
#
# THE CASE THIS PROVES: dispatching `Open` twice under the SAME `code`,
# the second time with a negative `balance`, is a duplicate identity AND
# a falsified invariant on the SAME dispatch. Ruby's own
# `hydrate_complete_state` (ATOMIC_PUT-eligible) defers its `AlreadyExists`
# check all the way to `step_save` — AFTER `apply_mutations` and
# `enforce_invariants` already ran — so it answers `InvariantViolation`,
# never `AlreadyExists`, for this exact combination. A fix that moved
# the deferred existence check to run BEFORE `enforce_invariants`
# instead of after (the "third order that exists nowhere in Ruby" a
# BUG#4-shaped mistake produces) would answer `AlreadyExists` here
# instead — this fixture is what catches that.
#
# `spec/corpus/rust_conformance/bug28_ensures_and_invariant_before_
# atomic_put_existence_check.json` is the differential harness step
# that actually dispatches this sequence against both engines.
Hecks.bluebook "Bug28ExistenceFixture" do
  vision "The smallest domain pairing a state-independent creating command with a genuinely-falsifiable aggregate invariant — the existence-vs-invariant ordering pair BUG#28's own real corpus example (Account.Open) can't exercise today."

  core

  aggregate "Vault" do
    description "A vault holding a starting balance, addressed by its own code — the balance is never defaulted, so its own invariant is genuinely checkable at creation."

    identified_by :code

    attribute :code, VaultCode
    attribute :balance, Cents

    value_object "VaultCode" do
      attribute :value, String, pattern: '[^ \t\n\r]'
      invariant("a code is not blank") { !value.to_s.empty? }
    end

    value_object "Cents" do
      attribute :value, Integer
    end

    invariant("a vault's balance never goes negative") { balance.value >= 0 }

    command "Open" do
      goal "Open a vault with a starting balance"

      attribute :code, VaultCode
      attribute :balance, Cents

      sets :code
      sets :balance

      emits "VaultOpened"
    end
  end
end
